claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he is still in approved education or training.

Could you tell me, is Alex currently in full-time approved education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or an equivalent qualification) or approved training that is unpaid?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that Alex is studying for his A-levels. A-levels count as approved education, which means you may still be eligible for Child Benefit for him until he turns 20, as long as he remains in approved education.

Now I have a couple more questions to check your eligibility:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

Next, could you confirm whether Alex lives with you, or if he lives elsewhere? If he lives elsewhere, are you contributing towards his upkeep (for example, paying for food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week in paid employment?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you.

One final question: Is Alex currently receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually he does receive Universal Credit in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that important detail.

Unfortunately, this affects your eligibility for Child Benefit. According to the rules, you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts receiving certain benefits in their own right, including Universal Credit.

Since Alex is receiving Universal Credit in his own name, this means you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him, even though he is under 20 and in approved education.

Let me provide you with the formal outcome of this assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm sorry to say that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Summary:**

| Child | Eligible? | Reason |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| Alex | No | Receives Universal Credit in his own name |

**Explanation:**

Although Alex meets several of the usual criteria for Child Benefit eligibility (he's under 20, in approved education studying A-levels, lives with you in the UK, and isn't working), the fact that he receives Universal Credit in his own name disqualifies you from claiming Child Benefit for him. The rules state that Child Benefit stops if the child starts receiving certain benefits, including Universal Credit.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he stops receiving Universal Credit), you may wish to reassess your eligibility at that time.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
